clue.text: Hitched a ride with Mr. Clumsy

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched and jumbled, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker gets a lift from an awkward, bumbling driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitched' reads as hitchhiking, but it is the slang sense of getting wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hitched is informal for to marry, so a hitched couple is a wedded couple.

clue.text: Cockney is not on English course

parts.note: ain't is the Cockney way of saying is not
re means on, as in concerning
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Londoner denies that something is happening on an English racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous horse-racing venue, so a racecourse is a fair description.

clue.text: Government accepting British currency abroad

indicators.note: one thing accepting another takes it in, so a letter sits inside the word for government

parts.note: rule is government, as in direct rule
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A government agrees to take sterling in place of foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruble (rouble) is the monetary unit of Russia, a foreign currency to a British solver.

clue.text: Former media state

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A former journalist describes the condition of the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun meaning condition; it is the verb, to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to state or voice it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Parties holding back numerous energetic folk

indicators.note: the parties hold the other word between their letters

parts.note: dos are parties or celebrations

indicators.note: holding something back here means turning it the wrong way round

parts.note: numerous means many

explanation.surface: Party organisers keep a lot of lively people at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is figuratively a forceful, tirelessly active person, so dynamos are energetic people.

clue.text: Long-lost article on country farmer?

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the definite article, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A long-forgotten newspaper piece about a farmer from some country.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a yeoman was a man who farmed his own land.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a yeoman was a small landowner who worked his own farm, so a farmer by definition.

clue.text: Perhaps setter's gonna tune out

indicators.note: a tune that is out is off key and wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler announces they are going to play a song badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' reads as the puzzle's compiler; here it is a word, an example of a noun formed from a verb to name the doer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent noun names the one who performs an action, like setter from set, so setter is an instance.

clue.text: Stellar group welcomes Alternative Technology lecture

indicators.note: a group that welcomes someone takes them in among its members

parts.note: Orion is a constellation, a group of stars
AT is the abbreviation for Alternative Technology

explanation.surface: A group of star performers invites a talk on green engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech or address, much like a lecture given to an audience.

clue.text: Again, covered heel protrudes improperly

indicators.note: something arranged improperly is set out wrongly, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoe's heel sticks out awkwardly even after another layer was added.
explanation.definitionFit: To reupholster is to put new padding and fabric on furniture, so the piece is covered once more.

clue.text: Backing screw for round handle

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: bonk is British slang for to have sex, as is screw

explanation.surface: A DIY instruction about which screw to use for fitting a round door handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' sounds like hardware next to 'handle', but it is the slang verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob is a rounded handle on a door or drawer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Positive new sign found in cure — remarkable

indicators.note: letters found in a word lie inside it, between its own letters

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for positive
to heal is to cure
N is the abbreviation for new
an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: A doctor finds an encouraging new indication in a treatment that is astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary or exceptional, a straight synonym of remarkable.

clue.text: As stated, releases stoppage

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: frees means releases

explanation.surface: An announcement that someone lets things go, causing a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze is a halt or suspension, as in a pay freeze or hiring freeze.

clue.text: Cash-crop estate needs to separate discarded fruit

indicators.note: the two letters are thrown out though they stand apart, not side by side, in the longer word

parts.note: a plantation is an estate growing cash crops such as sugar or cotton
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farm growing crops for sale has to sort out fruit it has thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: The T and O removed are not adjacent: drop the second T and the O of PLANTATION, leaving PLANTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit usually eaten cooked, grown widely in the tropics.

clue.text: Prepare for business session about returning deposit before operation

indicators.note: the session goes round the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: sesh is informal British for a session, often of drinking

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for deposit runs backwards

parts.note: to put something down is to deposit it
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a day's trading by banking money before a medical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up shop is an idiom for establishing a business or getting ready to trade.

clue.text: Plain girl one boy stood up — and another

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down answer standing something up turns it bottom to top, reading upwards

parts.note: Rod is a boy's name
Ned is another boy's name

explanation.surface: An unattractive girl was let down by one date, then by a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a description of the girl; it is the definition, simple and undecorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without ornament or embellishment, so simple and plain.

clue.text: Scrap outside trendy nightclub

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount, a scrap
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in front of a fashionable club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight outside a club, but it means a small bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is informal for a bar, club or other place of entertainment.

clue.text: Wife cuts bay tree

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word slices in between its letters

parts.note: bay and roan are both horses named for their coat colour, so one stands for the other
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife prunes a bay tree in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay tree' reads as one plant, but bay is a horse here and tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree bearing red berries.

clue.text: Mostly head around salt lake

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the other piece
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: onion is slang for the head
a salt and a tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: Heading mostly round a lake full of brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt lake' suggests brine, but Lake Ontario is fresh water; salt is the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America, on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: A transgression, initially shunning one and all, shows stupidity

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so those letters are kept out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a transgression
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An offence, avoiding everyone from the start, displays foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but the word itself is used: take I and ALL out of it to leave INITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Asininity is extreme foolishness, from asinine, literally donkey-like.

clue.text: Stole book in middle of excellent day

indicators.note: a letter in the middle of a word sits inside it

parts.note: noble means excellent or of fine quality
B is the abbreviation for book
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone pinched a book on a splendid day.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is British slang for to steal, so nobbled means stole.

clue.text: Apprentice, one on the railways?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person learning a trade
second meaning, playful: like an employee, a person put on a train

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical, reading the word as train plus -ee, someone the train carries; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being taught a job, the same as an apprentice.

clue.text: Drunk, heartless, is internally suffering

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so one piece goes within the other
without a heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: merry is British for tipsy, slightly drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted drunk is in pain on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is great distress or unhappiness, the state of suffering.

clue.text: Poison pirate on waves

indicators.note: waves toss things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pirate on the high seas uses poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, so a poison.

clue.text: Ruin sailors picked up behind bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: jacks, or jack tars, are sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen get collected from behind the pub counter and are wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: BANJAX is Irish-English slang for to ruin or wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To banjax something is to break or ruin it, so the words are interchangeable.

clue.text: Name abstainers — following one, a particular mess

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members abstain from drink
F is the abbreviation for following
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Teetotallers are named and followed into a particular muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI is the organisation running canteens for British forces; a mess is where service people eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A NAAFI canteen is a specific kind of forces' eating place, the military sense of mess.

clue.text: Zest displayed by running along clutching sword, having earlier crushed resistance

indicators.note: the letters clutch the sword, holding it inside
the resistance is crushed into the word first, squeezed in among its letters before the shuffle
running suggests letters set loose and moving about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Someone showing gusto by charging forward with sword in hand, having flattened opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The order matters: the resistance goes in before the letters are mixed, and only then does the result take the sword inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated outer rind of citrus fruit, so orange peel is a fair match.

clue.text: Complaint as green card partly withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the hidden run is read backwards
partly means only a portion of the words is used, a run hiding across them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of green and the start of card

explanation.surface: A US residence permit is partly revoked, prompting a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it is a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition, and complaint is used for any ailment or disorder.

clue.text: As has been noted, I don't like these 5 sports

definitions.text: As has been noted, I don't like these

indicators.note: sports as a verb can mean mutates or varies, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: the answer to 5-across

explanation.surface: A grumble about disliking the athletic pursuits of some team called 5.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at music: I Don't Like Mondays was a 1979 hit by the Boomtown Rats.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title completes the phrase, so the days in question are the start of the working week.

clue.text: Gallant American doctor contains problematic situation

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: the doctor contains the next word, holding it inside

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
a mire is a difficult situation, a mess one is stuck in

explanation.surface: A chivalrous US physician finds himself in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallant' looks like an adjective, but it is the old noun for a suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant, as a noun, is a man who courts a woman, her suitor or admirer.
